{{Short description|German physicist}}
'''Jürgen P. Rabe''' is a German [[physicist]] and [[nanoscientist]].

== Life ==
Jürgen P. Rabe studied [[physics]] and [[mathematics]] at [[RWTH Aachen University|RWTH Aachen]] where in 1981 he obtained his diploma in physics, based on a thesis on [[semiconductor]] [[optics]] with Peter Grosse. 1984 he obtained his [[doctorate|doctoral degree]] from the Department of Physics at the [[Technical University of Munich]], based on a [[biophysical]] thesis on model [[membrane]]s, promoted by [[Erich Sackmann]].

As a visiting scientist at the [[IBM Almaden Research Center]] in [[San José, California|San José]] (1984–1986) he initiated the use of [[scanning tunneling microscopy]] for [[molecular]] [[monolayer]]s, which he continued in Gerhard Wegner's department at the [[Max Planck Institute for Polymer Research]].

In 1992, he obtained his habilitation<ref>http://d-nb.info/943087414  Raster-Tunnelmikroskopie organischer Monoschichten : Struktur, Dynamik und elektronische Eigenschaften auf molekularer Skala / Jürgen P. Rabe </ref> on this topic and became a [[professor]] for [[physical chemistry]] at [[University of Mainz|Johannes Gutenberg-Universität]] in [[Mainz]]. Since 1994 Rabe is full professor for [[experimental physics]] with an emphasis on [[macromolecular]] and [[supramolecular chemistry|supramolecular]] systems at the Department of Physics at the [[Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin]]. Rabe is an elected scientific member of the [[Max Planck Society]] and external member of the [[Max Planck Institute of Colloids and Interfaces]] in [[Potsdam]]-Golm as well as founding director of the Integrative Research Institute for the Sciences IRIS Adlershof of Humboldt-Universität. He was visiting professor at the Materials Department of [[ETH Zürich]] and for the Department of Chemistry at [[Princeton University]].

Jürgen P. Rabe is the brother of [[:de:Klaus F. Rabe|Klaus F. Rabe]] and cousin of [[Sophia Rabe-Hesketh]] and the economist Birgitta Rabe.

== Research ==

Rabe became internationally known for his seminal [[Scanning tunneling microscope|scanning tunneling microscopy]] research on the structure, dynamics, and electronic properties of self-assembled molecular systems at solid-liquid interfaces.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Rabe|first1=Jürgen P.|last2=Buchholz|first2=Stefan|date=1991-07-12|title=Commensurability and Mobility in Two-Dimensional Molecular Patterns on Graphite|journal=Science|language=en|volume=253|issue=5018|pages=424–427|doi=10.1126/science.253.5018.424|issn=0036-8075|pmid=17746397|bibcode=1991Sci...253..424R|s2cid=42385720}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Rabe|first1=Jürgen P.|last2=Buchholz|first2=Stefan|date=1991|title=Direct observation of molecular structure and dynamics at the interface between a solid wall and an organic solution by scanning tunneling microscopy|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=66|issue=16|pages=2096–2099|doi=10.1103/physrevlett.66.2096|pmid=10043390|bibcode=1991PhRvL..66.2096R}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hentschke|first1=Reinhard|last2=Schürmann|first2=Britta L.|last3=Rabe|first3=Jürgen P.|date=1992-04-15|title=Molecular dynamics simulations of ordered alkane chains physisorbed on graphite|journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics|volume=96|issue=8|pages=6213–6221|doi=10.1063/1.462612|issn=0021-9606|bibcode=1992JChPh..96.6213H}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last1=Stabel|first1=Andreas|last2=Herwig|first2=Peter|last3=Müllen|first3=Klaus|last4=Rabe|first4=Jürgen P.|date=1995-08-18|title=Diodelike Current–Voltage Curves for a Single Molecule–Tunneling Spectroscopy with Submolecular Resolution of an Alkylated, peri-Condensed Hexabenzocoronene|journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition in English|language=en|volume=34|issue=15|pages=1609–1611|doi=10.1002/anie.199516091|issn=1521-3773}}</ref><ref>Jäckel, Frank; Watson, Mark D.; Müllen, Klaus; Rabe, Jürgen P.
